name: background-terminals
description: Run and manage long-lived shell commands in background terminals. Use for dev servers, watchers, streaming builds, and other commands that should keep running while the agent continues working.
---

# Background Terminals

Use `bg_start` for long-running commands; use regular `bash` for quick commands.

## Start

Call `bg_start` with:

- `command`: shell command to run
- `title`: short recognizable label
- `working_dir`: project directory when different from the current directory

Background commands receive no stdin. Never use them for interactive prompts.

After starting, continue useful work instead of polling. The terminal sends one completion message when it exits.

## Inspect and stop

- Use `bg_status` only when current output or status is needed.
- Use `bg_list` to inventory all tracked terminals.
- Use `bg_kill` when a process is no longer needed or is stuck; termination continues even if the tool wait is aborted.
- Tell the user they can open `/ps` to inspect live output and kill terminals interactively.

Prefer meaningful titles and avoid starting duplicate servers or watchers. Full output is captured to spill files; tool and completion output shows a concise tail. Terminals are session-scoped and are stopped during shutdown or reload.

// @vitest-environment node
/**
 * Rendered-layout regression for the UX-01 compact row (real Chrome, real CSS).
 *
 * This is the P1 guard for the compact conversation row at the 1000 CSS px
 * supported desktop breakpoint: with an unknown read state (and, in the worst
 * case, a pending membership operation) the row metadata was unbounded and
 * collapsed the subject/snippet column to zero width. jsdom has no layout, so
 * these assertions only mean something against real rendered CSS.
 *
 * The second P1 guard covers larger user text: at 1000px with a 20px root font
 * and the long old date label, the full inline metadata overflows the row, so
 * the adaptive compact presentation collapses the actions behind a named,
 * keyboard- and pointer-operable disclosure instead of trading subject
 * collapse for horizontal overflow.
 *
 * Opt-in only: set EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME to a Chrome/Chromium binary
 * path to run, e.g.
 *
 *   EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/path/to/chrome \
 *     pnpm vitest run tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts
 *
 * The test starts its own ephemeral Vite dev server and its own headless
 * Chrome profile (synthetic in-memory browser fake only — never real Gmail,
 * never real mail), and tears both down in `afterAll`. Default `pnpm test`
 * runs skip it (jsdom environment stays default).
 */
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createServer, type ViteDevServer } from 'vite';

const CHROME_ENV = 'EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME';
const chromePath = process.env[CHROME_ENV] ?? '';

interface Rect { left: number; right: number; top: number; bottom: number; width: number; height: number }
interface RowMeasure {
  innerWidth: number;
  clientMode: string | null;
  row: Rect;
  rowScrollWidth: number;
  rowClientWidth: number;
  listScrollWidth: number;
  listClientWidth: number;
  sender: Rect;
  subjectSnippet: Rect;
  subject: { left: number; right: number; width: number; visibleChars: number; truncated: boolean; text: string };
  meta: Rect;
  date: string | null;
  pending: { width: number; text: string } | null;
  readState: { width: number; text: string; test: string | null } | null;
  buttons: Array<{ name: string; test: string | null; visible: boolean } & Rect>;
  focusedButtons: Array<string | null>;
  toggle: { visible: boolean; ariaExpanded: string | null } & Rect | null;
  actionsPanel: { position: string; visibility: string; width: number } | null;
}

interface CdpSession {
  cmd(method: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any>;
  js<T>(expression: string): Promise<T>;
  close(): void;
}

describe.skipIf(chromePath === '')('InboxList rendered layout (real Chrome, opt-in)', () => {
  let server: ViteDevServer | null = null;
  let appUrl = '';
  let chrome: ReturnType<typeof spawn> | null = null;
  let profileDir: string | null = null;
  let cdp: CdpSession | null = null;
  let tornDown = false;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    server = await createServer({

      // Inline overrides win over vite.config.ts (whose fixed port could clash).

    });

    appUrl = server.resolvedUrls?.local?.[0] ?? '';

    );

# UX-05 — Select and process several conversations safely
Status: **implemented and integrated on `feat/ux-05-safe-bulk-processing` (synthetic validation only; see §9).**
Scoped against `ed6b2d2` after UX-04. Source requirements:
[UX spec](../superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md) §List focus, opening, and
selection, §Context precedence, BROWSE-06/18; delivery boundary:
[implementation plan](superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md) §UX-05.
Build on [UX-03](ux-03-command-discovery.md) and
[UX-04](ux-04-trustworthy-undo.md), not a new mutation engine.
Everything below is a proposed engineering contract (`P`). The spec documents
multiselect shortcuts and bulk actions (`D`), but not these exact range,
transaction, recovery, or partial-Undo semantics. This is not a claim of
Superhuman equivalence or authorization to mutate a real mailbox.
## 1. Deliverable and boundaries
```text
Select three conversations → see “3 selected” and explicit action labels
→ Done → one durable group receipt → per-member pending/confirmed/failed/unknown
→ recover individual failures in Activity, or Z within 10 s for eligible members
→ restart → group and member outcomes remain inspectable
```
**Ship together:**
- Independent account-scoped selection, range anchor, count, pointer and keyboard
  controls in Inbox and cached Done.
- Bulk Done/Not Done and explicit Mark read/Mark unread through the shared
  action catalog, with the existing capability gates. Read remains Gmail-only;
  native fixture mode covers archive/unarchive groups, like the current setters.
- Bounded, idempotent, transactional **local group acceptance**, member receipts,
  immutable message targets and per-message preimages.
- Per-member status/recovery and one-level group Undo, including honest partial
  results. Reuse the serial worker, provider setters and reconciliation.
**Do not include:** stars (the star portion of BROWSE-06 is deferred), labels,
move, trash, reminders, new provider permissions, multiple accounts/providers,
new browsing contexts, all-matching/cross-page selection, concurrent provider
execution, a Gmail batch endpoint, arbitrary action execution, HTML rendering,
auto-read, redo or multi-level Undo. No composer/send changes. No state-framework
or worker replacement. Selection itself need not survive restart; accepted
intent and its recovery records must.
## 2. Source facts and required changes
| Current source | UX-05 consequence |
|---|---|
| `useMailbox.ts` has `focusedRef`, `openRef`, stable-ID focus resolution and context/session fences, but no selection. | Add selected references and range anchor independently; reuse account/context fencing and focus fallback. |
| `InboxList.vue` uses list/listitem, roving focus and `aria-current`; plain click opens, row actions stop propagation. | Add explicit selection controls without conflating DOM focus with selected state or breaking compact-row overflow handling. |
| `App.vue::actionTarget` resolves one explicit/focused/reader target. | Replace shared conversation-action resolution with an immutable target list; explicit inline row actions still resolve exactly one row. |
| `submitMutation` and `inFlightCommandRef` track a single target; `LastAction`/`ActionNotice` describe one operation. | Introduce an explicit single-or-group pending/notice model; do not use the first selected ref as a fake group identity. |
| Gmail `accept_new_operation` opens a transaction around `accept_operation_tx`; fixture `Store::set_archived` owns its transaction. | Extract transaction-local acceptance helpers, retaining existing checks, for one bounded group transaction. Calling public setters in a loop is insufficient. |
| Gmail acceptance already persists immutable targets, effective per-message preimages and recovery snapshots; targets are bounded to 1000 messages per operation. | Preserve those limits/semantics for each member; never re-resolve inventory during execution, retry or Undo. |
| Both stores' Undo eligibility uses the newest non-compensating **operation**. | A loop would supersede every member except the last. Model a group as one top-level user action before exposing group Undo. |
| Activity contains individual operations, including recovery after rows leave Inbox; there is no durable group/query contract. | Persist group membership and expose group detail independently of current list rows and operation-history truncation. |
These are static source observations, not a new certification of existing code.
## 3. Selection and dispatch contract
### 3.1 State and exact interactions
Use account + conversation identity (`ConversationRef`), never indexes or a bare
conversation ID. Suggested state: `selectedRefs` (keyed set/map) and
`rangeAnchorRef`. Indexes are temporary inputs for movement/range calculation.
| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `X` on a list-owned focused row | Toggle that row, keep focus there, set range anchor there. Ignore auto-repeat. |
| Plain `J/K` (existing arrow aliases unchanged) | Move focus only, no wrap, no selection changes. |
| `Shift+J/K` | Move one row and add the inclusive anchor-to-destination range; if no valid anchor, start at the pre-move focused row. Boundary is a no-op. |
| Cmd-click row | Toggle that row and move focus/anchor there; do not open it. |
| Shift-click row | Add the inclusive anchor-to-clicked range and focus the clicked row; retain the anchor. If missing, use the pre-click focus, otherwise the clicked row alone. |
| Cmd+Shift-click | Same range behavior as Shift-click. |
| Row selection checkbox | Toggle only that row, set anchor there, never open it. |
| Plain row click / Enter | Existing open behavior; do not silently clear or widen selection. Enter on a native control retains native behavior. |
| Clear selection | Clear set and anchor, do not navigate. |
Range extension is **additive**: reversing direction does not subtract already
selected rows. This is a deliberate completion choice, not observed target
behavior. Date headings never participate. Hover never selects or marks read.
Provide **Select all loaded (N)** and **Clear selection** as discoverable pointer
controls and palette commands. Select-all snapshots only currently loaded rows,
not the exact-total count or unseen pages. Later page loads/new arrivals do not
join automatically. Proposed bound: **100 selected conversations per action**;
if more rows are loaded, disable Select all loaded with a visible explanation
and reject additions beyond 100 without replacing the existing selection. Never
silently take the first 100. This is a product/safety bound, not a provider limit.
### 3.2 Navigation and refresh
- Escape order: existing top overlay/disclosure/drawer → selected set → reader
  or context Back. Clearing selection does not also leave the current surface.
- Keep selection on reader open/return within the same browsing context, never
  extending it from reader J/K. Show its count and bulk scope in the reader too;
  hidden selection must never cause a surprising bulk action.
- Context/account changes clear selection and anchor; Back to a prior context
  restores navigation, **not** its old selected set. Disconnect/session changes
  fence outstanding receipts so old-account notices cannot repopulate the UI.
- A successful authoritative list refresh intersects selection with surviving
  loaded refs and clears an absent anchor. Loading/errors must not be mistaken
  for an authoritative empty result. Preserve existing stable-ID focus and scroll
  behavior; background refresh must not steal focus.
- At dispatch, freeze the exact selected references in current loaded order.
  The action's persisted member list, not the live selection, drives subsequent
  progress/recovery. Rows removed by a pending overlay may leave selection;
  they must not disappear from the group result surface.
- Definitively failed/rejected members stay reachable in Activity, even if no
  longer present in the active list. Provide per-item Open/Retry as applicable;
  never silently reselect them or include them in the user's next selection.
### 3.3 One target policy
Shared toolbar, palette and conversation-action shortcuts resolve:
1. Explicit inline row action → exactly that row, regardless of selected set.
2. Otherwise nonempty selection → exactly that set, even in the reader.
3. Otherwise existing focused/open conversation behavior.
Use the group path whenever selection is nonempty, even for one selected row.
Label selected-scope actions with the count; reader conversation triage controls
must use the same visible scope. Opening, copying contacts, message navigation,
and Reply are not bulk operations; Reply retains its existing source checks.
Bulk archive must not invoke single-reader “archive and advance” behavior.
Offer explicit **Mark N read** / **Mark N unread**, never a mixed-state toggle.
Existing inline single-row read toggling remains row-scoped. Selection actions
only intercept keys when the list owns them, and preserve IME, inputs,
contenteditable, buttons/links and top-surface precedence. No unconditional
global Cmd+A interception. Block duplicate mutation dispatch while acceptance
or its receipt recovery is unresolved; navigation can remain usable.
## 4. Durable group contract
### 4.1 Local acceptance is atomic; remote execution is not
A group contains one setter kind/value (archive, unarchive, read or unread)
and 1–100 unique refs from the active account. Validate structure, duplicates,
bounds, request ID, active account and capability before accepting anything.
Malformed/cross-account/unauthorized commands reject the whole request.
In **one SQLite transaction**:
1. Check a canonical fingerprint (kind, value, canonical member identities) and
   account-scoped group request ID. Same request/payload returns the original
   receipt; changed payload returns `request_id_conflict`. Preserve the original
   persisted member ordering on replay. Define collision handling with existing
   setter/Undo request IDs; no accidental cross-command receipt reuse.
2. Persist the group header, acceptance time and ordered member manifest.
3. For each member, accept an ordinary child operation with immutable message
   targets, effective preimages and recovery snapshot, using the existing checks.
   A member that is gone/unactionable or exceeds the existing target bound gets
   a persisted **rejected** acceptance result and typed reason, not a fabricated
   failed provider operation. Use prevalidation or member savepoints so rejected
   members leave no partial targets/preimages/request rows behind.
4. Persist the original receipt, including accepted operation IDs and rejected
   members; commit once. Wake the worker only after commit.
Storage/transaction failure rolls back **the entire local acceptance**. Even an
all-rejected valid request has an idempotent durable receipt, with zero child
operations. It does not supersede a previously undoable action. Accepted child

# UX-05 Rust/schema/Tauri/IPC safety review

**Verdict: needs attention.** Four actionable P2 findings.

Reviewed `ed6b2d2..80441d638645796aed166c69242ef25c6754a88d` against `docs/ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md`, using the supplied backend diff and current source. No edits, commits, or shell commands performed.

## Findings

### [P2] Include group tables in disconnect cleanup
**Location:** `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs:249–259`

The newly added group tables are not included in `clear_account()`, although that method deletes their operations, targets, requests, snapshots, and preimages (`1973–1991`). Accept a group, disconnect, and reconnect the same Google account: `list_operation_groups` returns the retained header/member manifest, but detail loading fails with `StorageUnavailable` because its accepted child operations no longer exist (`3240–3255`). Reusing the original request ID also bypasses request deduplication—the request row was deleted—and then fails the retained header’s unique constraint, causing Gmail admission to latch a storage halt. Delete headers and members in the same disconnect transaction as their backing records; test reconnect and original-request reuse.

### [P2] Return persisted group Undo decisions through the recovery query
**Location:** `crates/mail-core/src/groups.rs:146–151`

`OperationGroupStatus` exposes only the original acceptance receipt, original execution statuses, and current eligibility; neither store returns the persisted Undo decisions or compensation IDs. For example, undo a group where one confirmed member compensates and another is skipped for `UnknownPrior`, then restart or lose the Undo response: group detail reports both originals as confirmed and Undo as `AlreadyUndone`, with no way to inspect which member was skipped or recover the committed Undo receipt without the lost frontend-generated Undo request ID. This violates the required durable per-member recovery inspection; the ledger entry is not an approved deferral. Return the persisted Undo result through account-scoped group detail, with compensation linkage sufficient to inspect current compensation outcomes, and test restart and lost-response recovery.

### [P2] Populate the group linkage already declared on operation summaries
**Location:** `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs:2861–2864`; also `crates/mail-core/src/store.rs:1111–1114`

Both stores unconditionally set `OperationSummary.group_id` to `None`, including for accepted group children whose `action_id` contains the group identity. Thus the native IPC contract declares group linkage but never supplies it: ordinary Activity entries cannot identify their owning group, and failures lose that association when inspected outside the expanded recent-group manifest. Backend single-Undo checks correctly reject these children, so this is not an Undo authorization bypass, but the required operation-to-group recovery linkage is absent. Populate the field for children in both stores and assert it survives restart, while standalone operations and compensations remain ungrouped.

### [P2] Expose the persisted retry-to-member inspection link
**Location:** `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs:965–968`

Individual retries persist `retry_of`, but activity loading never selects or returns it, and neither group detail nor the generated DTOs expose an equivalent link. Retry a failed group member, let its retry confirm, then restart: group detail still correctly shows the historical member failure, but no returned record identifies the successful retry as its recovery. Multiple operations on the same conversation cannot establish that relationship reliably. The approved contract explicitly requires retries to remain linked to their original member for inspection; expose the persisted link additively and test a failed group member → confirmed retry → restart sequence without rewriting the original group receipt.

## Safety checks and coverage assessment

Source inspection supports the following implemented safeguards:

- Group acceptance uses one transaction, with per-member savepoints and whole-request propagation of storage failures.
- Canonical fingerprints preserve original receipt ordering on reordered replay; shared request tables distinguish group, setter, retry, and Undo payloads.
- Gmail group setters use the existing lifecycle, account, and mutation-capability admission path.
- Execution and compensation reuse persisted targets/preimages rather than expanding targets from current inventory.
- Transactional operation sequence—not timestamps—orders singles, groups, and ordinary member retries.
- Individual child Undo is rejected; expiry and supersession are enforced in Rust.
- Group cancellation and worker claims use the same connection mutex. Compensation is not assigned a new top-level action identity.
- Tauri exposes five narrow commands with explicit main-window permissions; forwarding preserves typed results/errors.

**Coverage gaps verified in the added tests:**

- **No actual mid-group storage-failure injection.** Both group rollback tests enable persistence failure before calling acceptance (`store.rs:2802` vicinity; `gmail/store.rs:5233`). Failure occurs at `persistence_gate()`, before opening the acceptance transaction—not after a child/preimage write. These tests do not demonstrate rollback of partially staged groups.
- **No controlled worker-claim versus group-Undo race test.** Store tests claim/confirm/fail sequentially; core tests wait for confirmation before Undo. Shared locking is structurally reassuring, but concurrency has not been exercised as claimed.
- Fixture restart coverage exists (`lib.rs:544–586`), but its group-Undo assertion checks only `AlreadyUndone`, not recovery of per-member decisions or compensation outcomes.
- Added Gmail group tests do not cover group reopen/restart, disconnect/reconnect cleanup, mixed-preimage group compensation, or failed/unknown compensation recovery.
- The migration fixture primarily restamps an already-current schema as version 2; it does not itself exercise adding missing UX-05 columns to an authentic version-2 profile.
- Transport tests verify command envelopes and typed rejection normalization, not actual native/provider convergence.

Tests were **not rerun by this read-only reviewer**. The implementation ledger records passing synthetic gates; those results are not independent runtime evidence from this review.

## Residual runtime validation

Before claiming native/provider acceptance, retain the documented operator checks:

- macOS/WKWebView fixture validation, including restart recovery and VoiceOver announcements.
- Real-browser rendered layout/focus regression; the ledger reports the opt-in suites skipped.
- Gmail archive/read-group convergence and compensation using only the approved disposable account and explicit modify grant.

After corrections, the supervisor should rerun the core suite, generated-contract check, and native bridge checks, adding deterministic mid-transaction failure and controlled claim/Undo interleaving tests.

## Human Reviewer Callouts (Non-Blocking)

- **This change adds a database migration:** Both stores gain durable group/member tables and operation action/retry linkage; fixture schema advances to version 3 and Gmail declares `gmail-2`.
- **This change modifies auth/permission behavior:** Five explicit operation-group command permissions are granted to the main Tauri window in `src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json`. Provider mutation authority is not broadened.

# UX-05 frontend / fake / transport review

**Verdict: needs attention.**

Reviewed `ed6b2d2..80441d638645796aed166c69242ef25c6754a88d` against `docs/ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md`, using the supplied exact diffs and current source. This was read-only; I ran no commands or tests.

Both follow-up observations are confirmed: **Dismiss releases the unresolved-acceptance fence and discards the retained request**, and **Activity discards pagination cursors, making older groups undiscoverable through the UI**.

## Findings

### 1. [P1] Preserve unresolved requests when dismissing their notice
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:1069–1071`

`ActionNotice.vue:200–203` exposes **Dismiss** specifically for `acceptance-unknown`, but this function only checks `groupInFlight` before deleting `lastGroup`. Once the rejected round trip finishes, dismissing removes the original request ID and immutable command and makes `bulkUnresolved` false. If acceptance committed but both its response and lookup were lost, the user can now submit another group with a fresh request ID instead of recovering the original. Retain unresolved intent independently of notice visibility, or disallow dismissal until acceptance is resolved (§3.3/§4.3).

### 2. [P1] Prevent group dispatch while a single mutation is awaiting acceptance
**Location:** `src/App.vue:99–103`

`bulkMembers()` checks `bulkUnresolved` but not `inFlightCommandRef`; selected-scope availability also returns before `actionTarget()` supplies the existing single-command guard. Consequently, after starting an inline single-row action, the user can immediately click the selection bar action. The group increments `commandToken`, so the original single's `finally` at `useMailbox.ts:823–825` no longer clears `inFlightCommandRef`. After both calls complete, single actions and reader controls can remain permanently disabled, and the late single receipt can replace the newer group notice. Apply the pending-command fence to group dispatch at both UI and composable boundaries.

### 3. [P1] Fence and clear group recovery data across account sessions
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:1007–1012`

`refreshRecentGroups()` writes its response without checking the captured account/session or a request token. `openGroupDetail()` likewise checks only its detail token, which disconnect/account-change handling never invalidates. Neither transition clears `recentGroups` or `groupDetail`. An old-account response can therefore repopulate Activity after disconnect/reconnect, or already-loaded old groups can remain visible until another successful group fetch. Clear these surfaces and invalidate their requests alongside ordinary Activity; check the session before accepting responses (§3.2).

### 4. [P2] Persist the initial fallback range anchor
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:604–606`

When no explicit anchor exists, `extendSelectionTo()` uses the fallback only for that call and never saves it in `rangeAnchorRef`. For example, start on row 1, Shift+J to row 2, move with plain J to row 6, then Shift+K to row 5: the implementation selects rows 1–2 and 5–6 instead of extending from the original row-1 anchor through row 5. Establish the initial anchor when the first range is accepted, including the target-only case (§3.1).

### 5. [P2] Replace reader single-state toggles with explicit selected-scope controls
**Location:** `src/App.vue:1482–1485`

The reader now dispatches its controls to the selection, but `ReaderView.vue:617–628` still chooses a single read/unread toggle from the **open conversation's** read state. With a mixed selection and a read conversation open, the reader offers only “Mark unread”; it does not offer explicit “Mark N read” and “Mark N unread.” The archive toggle similarly derives its operation from the open conversation rather than selected scope and can emit an unavailable bulk action when reader state and originating context differ. The banner discloses scope, but does not satisfy the explicit desired-state/count-labelled reader-control contract (§3.3).

### 6. [P2] Follow Activity group pagination instead of dropping older receipts
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:1010–1012`

Only the newest ten groups are fetched and `nextCursor` is discarded; neither `Mailbox` nor `ActivityPanel` exposes a continuation control or request-ID lookup input. After eleven all-rejected groups and a restart, the oldest rejection receipt has no child operation in ordinary Activity and cannot be discovered or opened anywhere in the UI. Accepted groups also lose their grouped receipt/Undo inspection once outside this page. Preserve the cursor and expose bounded pagination, while retaining direct detail addressability (§4.2/§6).

### 7. [P2] Refresh expanded group detail when operation state changes
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:443–447`

Mailbox refresh updates group summaries and the notice slot, but never refreshes an expanded `groupDetail`. Open a group while its children are queued and allow them to finish: its detail continues showing queued members, stale Undo availability, and no Retry buttons even after failures. Detail only reloads after another explicit open or group Undo. Refresh the expanded request on authoritative change events, with appropriate ordering/session fences (§6).

### 8. [P2] Surface group recovery read failures instead of treating them as absence
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:1224–1226`

`openGroupDetail()` converts every lookup failure into `null`; the group stays expanded with no detail, error, or retry explanation. The new recent-group and status fetches use equivalent silent fallbacks, so a failed initial group-history read can render “No operations yet,” while a failed status read can leave an accepted group labelled “Accepting…”. These are recovery boundaries, not optional decoration: distinguish loading, absence, stale data, and failure, and expose a retry path rather than silently hiding persisted recovery records.

### 9. [P2] Track compensation outcomes instead of displaying “restoring” indefinitely
**Location:** `src/components/ActionNotice.vue:86–88`

After group Undo, notice wording depends only on the immutable number of `compensating` decisions. It always appends “restoring…” whenever that count is nonzero, even after compensation confirms, fails, or becomes outcome-unknown. Unlike single-action Undo, the group view never resolves the returned compensation operation IDs to current statuses. A failed restoration is therefore hidden behind permanent pending wording. Track and announce compensation outcomes separately from original execution (§5/§6).

### 10. [P2] Expose persisted group Undo decisions through the restart-query seam
**Location:** `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts:147–155`

`OperationGroupStatus` returns the original receipt, original child statuses, and Undo availability, but not the persisted group Undo receipt, skip reasons, or compensation identities. After restarting following partial Undo, Activity can only say “undo accepted”/“already undone”; a confirmed original child cannot reveal whether restoration was queued, skipped for unknown prior state, or failed. The implementation ledger explicitly acknowledges this limitation, but the approved contract requires durable per-member Undo inspection and compensation recovery (§4.2/§5/§6). Add this data to an addressable query and render it in detail.

### 11. [P2] Expose retry lineage for group-member recovery inspection
**Location:** `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts:261–269`

The added operation linkage exposes `groupId`, but not the persisted retry-of relationship acknowledged in the implementation ledger. Retrying a failed group member creates a standalone operation; the original member remains failed, and neither its detail nor the retry row identifies the relationship. With repeated actions on the same conversation, the user cannot tell which result belongs to which recovery attempt. Expose retry lineage and provide a linked inspection route without rewriting the historical member result (§4.3).

### 12. [P2] Make loaded-selection bounds reactive
**Location:** `src/components/SelectionBar.vue:34–37`

`selectAllDisabled` and `selectAllTitle` are plain setup constants derived from `loadedCount`. If the bar mounts with 100 loaded Done rows and another page loads, “Select all loaded (200)” remains enabled with the original title. Conversely, a bar mounted above the limit can remain disabled after refresh reduces the loaded set to an allowed size. The composable safely refuses an oversized selection, but the discoverable control's enabled state and explanation are wrong. Derive both values reactively.

### 13. [P2] Do not overwrite newer notice state with a captured status-refresh slot
**Location:** `src/composables/useMailbox.ts:999–1003`

`refreshGroupStatus()` spreads the slot captured **before** its await back into `lastGroup`, checking only request identity. A delayed status read started before Undo can finish after `undoGroupById()` records its receipt and overwrite `undone` with the captured `null`; a pre-Undo response can also restore stale Undo availability. The notice then loses the accepted partial-Undo result or offers Undo again. Fence status responses and merge into the current slot rather than restoring stale local fields.

### 14. [P2] Restrict selection shortcuts to actual list ownership
**Location:** `src/App.vue:1181–1186`

`selectionKeysOwned` excludes reader/buttons but does not check whether the list owns focus, unlike the nearby `browsingOwns` predicate. This is reachable without synthetic events: resizing from the narrow contact disclosure to the wide layout explicitly focuses `contactColumnEl` at line 439. Pressing X or Shift+J/K there changes the hidden list selection, although the contact surface owns focus. Use an actual list/body ownership predicate, retaining input, IME, and top-surface guards (§3.3).

### 15. [P2] Restore focus when Clear removes the focused selection bar
**Location:** `src/App.vue:148–150`

Clicking or keyboard-activating Clear calls only `clearSelection()`, which removes the entire selection bar and its focused button. No focus handoff runs; the list's focus-restoration watcher does not observe selection changes. DOM focus consequently falls back to the document instead of the focused row or empty-list surface. Hand focus to a surviving surface after the update without navigating (§6).

### 16. [P2] Match fake Undo availability to per-member eligibility
**Location:** `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts:599–605`

The fake reports `undo.available: true` whenever group-level ordering/time checks pass, even if every accepted child has definitively failed or has an unknown outcome. `groupUndoBlocker()` only checks that some child was originally accepted. Thus an all-failed group offers enabled Undo and accepts an all-skipped attempt, contrary to the explicit “all-ineligible group offers no enabled Undo” contract. Include current per-member eligibility in availability so preview behavior and frontend tests do not certify the wrong interaction (§5).

## Test gaps and validation limits

The existing tests cover useful basic selection, selected-one dispatch, row-action propagation, recovery replay, partial wording, and eligible-group restart cases. They do **not** exercise the critical scenarios above:

- Lost response **after commit**, failed lookup, Dismiss, and attempted fresh dispatch.
- Pending inline single followed by selected-scope group dispatch.
- Delayed group list/detail/status responses across disconnect or Undo.
- Initial range selection without X/checkbox establishing an anchor, followed by independent focus movement.
- Native pointer focus ordering for first Shift-click without an anchor.

### resume

`resume` revives a paused, completed, or failed async/foreground child by starting a new child from its stored session file. Stopped runs remain non-resumable, and it does not interrupt a live top-level async child. Use `steer` for acknowledged live async guidance.

- Multi-child async runs and remembered foreground single, parallel, or chain runs can be revived by passing `index` to choose the child.
- Nested runs can be resumed by nested id when their live route or persisted nested session metadata is available.
- Completed external-job runs, including nested runs, can use the same `resume` action as a provider follow-up when the registered provider exposes `followUp(input)`. Running external-job parents fail closed with guidance to wait for completion. Unsupported providers fail with an update/reload message.
- Revive starts a new child session from the old session context; it does not resume the live session, and it requires the chosen child to have a persisted `.jsonl` session file.
- Direct revival takes an exclusive cross-process lease on the canonical session file until the new child finishes. A concurrent attempt fails before Pi is spawned and identifies the owning revived run; dead-owner leases are reclaimed only when staleness can be proved.
- Without `message` (and without `index` or `chain`), `resume` on a top-level async workflow run that stopped because its session was replaced or its Pi process exited (`workflow.stopCause: "runtime-replaced"` or `"owner-exited"`) relaunches it once from the launch it saved, reusing its finished children, and its receipt starts with `Resumed workflow '<id>' as <new id>.`; a run that cannot be resumed is refused as `Cannot resume workflow '<id>': <reason>.` The session that owns the run also resumes it on its own when reopened or reloaded, unless [`autoResume`](configuration.md#autoresume) is off; see [Workflows](workflows.md).

content.text:
### steer

`steer` waits up to three seconds for a correlated receipt and returns a request id with `delivered`, `scheduled`, `pending`, `partial`, `recovered`, or `failed` plus per-child states. The receipt also has `deliveryStatus: "delivered" | "queued"`. For async runs, delivery means the child consumed the correlated user input; foreground delivery means the in-process Pi transport accepted it. Neither means model compliance. A pending indexed child returns `scheduled`.

The optional `mode` is `steer` by default and keeps the current interrupt behavior. `follow_up` waits for the next turn boundary. `auto` uses the same native steer delivery path as `steer`, without automatic pause-and-revive recovery after a missed acknowledgment. The retained revival-brief queue holds 20 messages and returns a clear error when full; this is not a live follow-up queue bound. A live follow-up acknowledgment reports queue acceptance, not consumption. Async runs later record correlated consumption or fail unconsumed requests at settlement; foreground follow-ups have no later correlated receipt. A `follow_up` sent to a completed retained workflow child becomes the first brief for its next `resume`; it does not revive the child by itself.

Only a top-level single run may interrupt after the acknowledgment deadline and recover after a further 15-second pause/revival bound; durable multi-child and nested runs never auto-interrupt. Recovery launches a replacement only after the source is confirmed paused, a valid persisted session exists, and deadline, turn, and tool budgets remain. It preserves the original child contract and remaining limits; otherwise the source stays paused with an explicit failure. Late acceptance is recorded but cannot cancel committed recovery.

The persisted `steering` ledger retains 20 requests and replaces the old `steerCount`/`lastSteerAt` fields.

The `/subagents-steer <run-id> [--child <child-id>] <message>` slash command is the host bridge for non-TUI sessions and RPC hosts. `--child` accepts the stable child identity shown in status output and inspect replies (workflow key, child run id, or `step:<index>`) and resolves it to the child index before steering; unknown or ambiguous child ids fail closed. Flags are parsed only between the run id and the message tail — once the message starts, `--` tokens are message text. The bridge always disables pause-and-revive recovery (`steeringRecovery: false`), matching the extension RPC `nonRecoveringSteer` guarantee so the caller keeps authority over the exact child it addressed.
